title: Practical Single Domain Generalization via Training-time and Test-time Learning

problem.claim: Single domain generalization seeks models that generalize to unseen target domains using a related source domain.

gap.claim: Existing methods mainly improve generalization during training and may perform unsatisfactorily after deployment under large domain shifts.

contributions.claim: PSDG combines training-time source-domain learning with test-time adaptation using unlabeled target-domain data.
During training, PSDG uses style generation, style-diversity regularization, and object-consistency regularization to expand training-domain coverage and filter style knowledge.
During testing, PSDG applies sample-aware and sharpness-aware minimization to optimize the model toward a flat entropy minimum surface using unlabeled target-domain knowledge.

stated_novelty.claim: The paper introduces StyIN as a newly proposed style generator for generating novel domain data.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on three real-world datasets are reported to demonstrate PSDG's effectiveness relative to several state-of-the-art methods.

narrative_sequence.summary: Single domain generalization targets unseen-domain generalization from a related source domain.
Training-focused methods can struggle under large target-domain shifts.
PSDG expands training diversity and enforces object consistency through StyIN and two regularizers.
PSDG adapts using unlabeled target data through sample-aware and sharpness-aware minimization.
The authors report effectiveness on three real-world datasets against several state-of-the-art methods.

source_observation.claim: The method combines training-time domain diversification with test-time adaptation using unlabeled target data.

interpretation.claim: Robustness to domain shift is addressed through both broader training coverage and deployment-time adjustment.

application.claim: For deployment settings with unlabeled target data, consider pairing source-domain generalization with constrained test-time adaptation.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this approach is appropriate when unlabeled target-domain data are unavailable.

unknowns: The three datasets and their domains are not identified.
Quantitative results, evaluation metrics, and comparison outcomes are not reported.
The compared state-of-the-art methods are not named.
The abstract does not specify the exact test-time update procedure or adaptation constraints.
